_about: What goes in the claude.ai developer portal for the main pflow connector. Matt submits it; nothing reads this file at run time. cmd/webserver/mcp_directory_test.go holds it to the server and to public/mcp.html. Gates and remaining steps: checklist.md.
name: pflow
one_liner: Snap parts together into a system you can see, run and check, with a stable ID to cite every model by.
description:
Snap parts together into a working system and find out whether it holds up before you build it.

Start from a catalog of parts (a bounded queue, a resource pool, a two-step saga with compensation) or bring your own models. Ask which connections are legal, join the parts, then run scenarios to see what happens when a payment fails or a second order arrives.

The answers come from an engine, not an estimate: whether the system can deadlock, what it always conserves, how the outcome moves when one rate changes, and a replayable counterexample when a property fails.

Every model has a content ID, so the same model always gets the same citation, and a link opens a net in the pflow.xyz editor.

Every tool except saving works without an account. Saving needs a GitHub or Google sign-in, and saved models are public.

gates.copy_when_open: Snap parts together on a canvas right in the conversation: pick a port, the legal joins light up, and every join is checked as you make it.
Look up a verified part by concept and get the model, its invariants and the theorem or paper behind it, with a stable CID to cite.

example_prompts.prompt: Join an order queue, a worker pool and a payment saga with pflow, show me which links the queue's dequeue could take, then run the failed-payment scenario.
Model two philosophers sharing two forks with pflow and tell me whether they can deadlock.
What stays constant in this pflow model? Give me a link to open it.
Here's my pflow model. Simulate it to t=50 and tell me where everything ends up.

use_cases: Design a system from reusable parts and check that the joins are legal
Find deadlocks and prove what a system conserves before building it
Compare what-if scenarios on a seeded, repeatable simulation
prerequisites: None. Saving asks for a GitHub or Google sign-in the first time.
data_access: Reads and writes: every tool works on the model in the call, and pflow_save stores a net publicly.
